findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a Layer W unit test proving a `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` comment silences an otherwise-failing tracker-context git mutation in a workflow run-block/shell script, and state whether the YAML marker must be same-line or anywhere-in-step.
evidence: Plan states the marker works via '`# raw-git-ok: <reason>` comment lines in YAML/shell'
Testing (W) enumerates: cd+git add -A fails, git -C .tickets-tracker commit fails, bare git commit passes, working-directory + mutation fails — but no marked-workflow-passes case
Python marker suppression IS tested ('same line with # raw-git-ok: reason passes'); the YAML/shell suppression path is asserted but unproven
findings.finding: The Testing section proves the Layer W marker only implicitly: it tests that tracker-context git mutations FAIL and that a no-tracker-context step passes, but never proves that a `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` comment line SUPPRESSES a tracker-context git mutation in a workflow/shell block, even though the plan asserts markers work 'in YAML/shell'.
findings.location: Testing section (W) cases; Approach 'raw-git-ok: <reason> comment lines in YAML/shell'
scenarios: A workflow step that legitimately must issue a raw tracker-context git op (e.g. a seam-internal migration hook) adds the marker but the lint's YAML/shell suppression has a bug and still fails CI, blocking a valid change
Reviewer cannot confirm the marker's scope in YAML (same-line vs anywhere-in-step) from the plan
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Testing (W): 'a `cd .tickets-tracker` + `git add -A` step carrying a preceding `# raw-git-ok: seam-internal` comment PASSES', and specify the marker's positional scope for YAML/shell (same physical line as the git verb, or anywhere within the step/script block).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either add push/fetch/merge/stash/init to the R1 mutation-verb set (or justify their exclusion in the lint header/ACCEPTED RESIDUAL), and correct the sandbox-rationale claim that 'ALL of them get flagged by default' — since raw `git init`/`git fetch` (gerrit_client.py:360/367) match no current verb and do not fire R1.
evidence: gerrit_client.py:360 raw `subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", dest])` and :367 raw `git -C <dest> fetch ...` write a repo but match NO verb in the set → do not fire R1, yet the plan asserts 'ALL of them get flagged by default and the first two categories carry the marker'

push.py:168 `_git(base_path, "push", ...)`, :195 `fetch`, :214/:240 `merge`, :227 `stash push`; _ref_lock.py:760 `["push", "--force-with-lease=..."]` — real sanctioned tracker-write verbs absent from the R1 set (caught today only transitively via the R2 name-set, not R1)
A future raw `subprocess.run(["git","-C",tracker,"push"/"merge",...])` in a new module — with no named wrapper — would stay green under R1, a bypass of the same class the lint exists to stop
findings.finding: The R1 mutation-verb set (add/commit/rm/mv/reset/update-ref/checkout/clean) omits push/fetch/merge/stash/init, so a raw subprocess git write using those verbs is NOT flagged by Layer P R1 — contradicting the Approach's sandbox rationale that 'ALL of them get flagged by default'.
findings.location: Approach — Layer P R1 verb list; 'Rationale for module-agnostic flagging' paragraph ('ALL of them get flagged by default')
scenarios: New module issues raw `git push origin HEAD:tickets` or `git merge <tracker-ref>` via subprocess.run without a shared wrapper name — R1 does not fire
Reviewer reading the sandbox rationale trusts 'ALL flagged' but raw init/fetch in gerrit_client are silently unflagged
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the R1 (and W) mutation-verb set to include push/fetch/merge/stash (and optionally init/clone) at the subcommand position, OR explicitly scope the verb set to index/ref-mutating verbs and rewrite the 'ALL of them get flagged' sentence to 'every INDEX/REF mutation is flagged; network/init verbs against disposable clones are out of scope' so the claim matches the rule.

evidence: 3 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name _store/push.py and _store/sync.py as store-write seams (their local `_git` fires R2 by name for push/fetch/merge/reset/stash under the write lock) in the Context seam list and the Scope marker enumeration, so their expected report-scan hits are pre-dispositioned.
evidence: push.py:60 `def _git(base, *args, ...)` and sync.py:61 `def _git(tracker, *args)` — `_git` is in the plan's R2 name-set, so every caller fires R2 by name

push.py performs locked `push`/`fetch`/`merge`/`stash push`/`stash pop` (lines 168–262); sync.py `_do_reconverge` performs locked `reset --hard` (:155) and `_union_merge` — genuine tracker mutations under write_lock

Scope enumerates 'gitutil, event_append, txn, purge_bridge, reconciler git_adapter + _ref_lock' and maintenance callers delete/compact/txn/init/fsck/fsck_repair/fsck_recover, but NOT push.py or sync.py
Context frames the write surface as exactly two seams (store + reconciler) — push.py's best-effort push/reconverge and sync.py's reconverge are a third locked-mutation family not named
findings.finding: The Context 'two sanctioned seams' framing and the Scope marker enumeration omit _store/push.py and _store/sync.py, which are store-write seams (locked push/fetch/merge/reset/stash against the tracker) that the report-mode scan will flag via the R2 `_git` name.
findings.location: Context ('The REAL write surface has two sanctioned seams') and Scope (marker enumeration bullet)
scenarios: Report-mode scan flags push.py:168/sync.py:155 callers; author consulting the plan's prose enumeration finds no entry and is unsure whether these are expected hits or new bypasses
findings.suggested_fix: Add push.py/sync.py to the Scope marker bullet ('# raw-git-ok: locked store seam internal') and note in Context that the store seam includes the push/reconverge paths (push.py, sync.py) alongside the transaction/append layers.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `_store/sync.py` (`_git` caller sync.py:155 `reset --hard`) and `_store/push.py` (`_git` callers push.py:100-101 `rm --cached` / `checkout HEAD`) to the enumerated seam-internal `# raw-git-ok: locked store seam internal` marker inventory, re-deriving the full `_git`-wrapper set with `find_referencing_symbols`/a `def _git` sweep across `_store` rather than the hand list.
evidence: Plan (Scope): 'the store-maintenance callers of per-module `_git` wrappers (delete, compact, txn, init, fsck, fsck_repair, fsck_recover)'

Plan (Approach, R2): '_git ... a name defined locally in at least eight modules — _commands/delete.py:173, compact.py:58, txn.py:119, init.py:80, fsck.py:386, fsck_repair.py:56, fsck_recover.py:61, opcert_service/workspace.py'
Omitted: src/rebar/_store/sync.py:61 `def _git(tracker, *args)` with caller sync.py:155 `_git(tracker, "reset", "--hard", remote, "--quiet")`

Omitted: src/rebar/_store/push.py:60 `def _git(base, *args)` with callers push.py:100 `_git(base, "rm", "-q", "--cached", "--", *unmerged)` and push.py:101 `_git(base, "checkout", "HEAD", "--", *unmerged)`
src/rebar/_store/sync.py docstring: 'the reset/merge that mutate HEAD run UNDER the unified write lock' — confirms these are locked store-seam mutations needing the seam-internal marker
findings.finding: The plan's enumerated inventory of local `_git`-wrapper store-maintenance modules (delete/compact/txn/init/fsck/fsck_repair/fsck_recover) omits two sibling `_git` wrappers in the same `_store` package — `src/rebar/_store/sync.py:61` and `src/rebar/_store/push.py:60` — whose callers pass tracker-targeting mutation verbs that the plan's own R2 rule fires on. sync.py:155 calls `_git(tracker, "reset", "--hard", remote, "--quiet")`; push.py:100-101 call `_git(base, "rm", "-q", "--cached", ...)` and `_git(base, "checkout", "HEAD", ...)`. `_git` is in the plan's R2 name-set and `reset`/`rm`/`checkout` are in its mutation-verb list, so R2 will fire unmarked at enforcement. These are locked store-seam mutations (sync.py docstring: the reset/merge "run UNDER the unified write lock"), i.e. exactly the `# raw-git-ok: locked store seam internal` category — not sandbox. A `def _git` grep across `_store` surfaces them, so the enumeration was not derived from the full symbol/name graph.
findings.location: Scope, bullet 2 ('the store-maintenance callers of per-module `_git` wrappers (delete, compact, txn, init, fsck, fsck_repair, fsck_recover)') and the R2 named-caller list in Approach
scenarios: src/rebar/_store/sync.py:155 (`reset --hard`) — R2 fires unmarked; if not dispositioned, the report-mode bootstrap PR either leaves an unmarked hit (lint fails at enforcement) or the site is missed until the full scan, contradicting the Scope's own explicit marker list
src/rebar/_store/push.py:100-101 (`rm --cached` / `checkout HEAD`) — R2 fires unmarked on a locked store-seam path; missing from the enumerated seam-internal marker set
The plan claims the store seam's mutation surface but its named inventory misses the sync/push reconvergence layer, so a reviewer relying on the prose list under-scopes the marker work
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the Scope marker inventory and R2 named-caller list to include the `_store/sync.py` and `_store/push.py` local `_git` wrappers and their mutation-verb callers (sync.py:155 reset; push.py:100-101 rm/checkout), tagging them `# raw-git-ok: locked store seam internal`, and re-derive the wrapper/caller set from the symbol graph so no sibling `_git` in `_store` is missed.

findings.finding: The plan's load-bearing premise 'The raw sites at HEAD are few and verified' is materially false: many additional legitimate store-write sites route through per-module local _git wrappers (which themselves call run_git_write) and will fire under R2's by-name flagging, each needing a marker the plan does not enumerate.
findings.location: Approach — 'The raw sites at HEAD are few and verified'; Scope — 'inline markers on the enumerated seam internals'; AC line 'All enumerated seam internals ... are marked with reasons; tree is clean at landing'
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the fixed 5-site enumeration with an instruction to enumerate every raw/wrapped mutation site by running the two rules across the tree first, and expand the marker-target list in Scope to include _commands/delete.py, compact.py, txn.py (STATUS/CLAIM callers), init.py bootstrap, fsck_repair.py, fsck_recover.py.

findings.finding: The plan claims raw-git disposable-sandbox writes have exactly 'two known sites' (eval_solver.py, criterion_preview.py), but at least two more Python sites issue a FLAGGED mutation verb (checkout) against disposable clone workspaces and are not enumerated: src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py:374 (`git checkout FETCH_HEAD`) and src/rebar/opcert_service/workspace.py:108 (`git checkout -q -B ...`) plus :125 (`git worktree add`). Layer P (module-agnostic) WILL flag these, so they must be marked or remediated, but they are absent from the first-scan marker list.
findings.location: Approach — 'two known sites' rationale; Scope — inline marker enumeration; Testing — 'Full-tree run is clean at merge'
findings.suggested_fix: Rescope the sandbox enumeration to name eval_solver.py, criterion_preview.py, review_bot/gerrit_client.py, and opcert_service/workspace.py (the `_git`/`_git_ok` wrapper functions), each getting `# raw-git-ok: disposable clone/workspace, not the tracker`; replace 'two known sites' with the accurate count.

findings.finding: The plan's enumeration of store-seam-internal modules to mark ('gitutil, lock, event_append, txn, purge_bridge, migration/bootstrap, reconciler git_adapter + _ref_lock') omits two verified tracker-writing seam internals — src/rebar/_store/push.py and src/rebar/_store/sync.py — each of which fires under the plan's OWN Layer-P R2 rules but is not listed among the internals to receive a `# raw-git-ok:` marker.
findings.location: Scope bullet 2 ('inline # raw-git-ok markers on the enumerated seam internals (gitutil, lock, event_append, txn, purge_bridge, migration/bootstrap, reconciler git_adapter + _ref_lock)'); Approach '_git — the four wrapper names at HEAD'
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope bullet 2, extend the seam-internal list to '…gitutil, lock, event_append, txn, purge_bridge, push, sync, migration/bootstrap, reconciler git_adapter + _ref_lock'; mark push.py/sync.py's `_git` bodies and their locked mutation call sites with `# raw-git-ok: locked store seam internal`, and update the R2 wrapper-name discussion to note `_git` is defined in three modules (_ref_lock, push, sync).

findings.finding: The Scope's committed inventory of seam internals to mark ("gitutil, lock, event_append, txn, purge_bridge, migration/bootstrap, reconciler git_adapter + _ref_lock") is incomplete: a codebase sweep for git mutation verbs finds several locked-store-write command internals with their own `_git()` wrappers that are neither enumerated nor covered by the named buckets — delete.py, compact.py, and fsck_repair.py. Each mutates the tracker under the write lock, so each will be flagged by Layer P and must carry a `# raw-git-ok: locked store seam internal` marker, but none is named as a marking target. The plan's Rationale further asserts "every raw mutation is a seam internal, a sandbox fixture, or a bypass", yet opcert_service/workspace.py and review_bot/gerrit_client.py issue raw mutations (worktree/remote add, checkout) that fit none of the three categories.
findings.location: Scope: "inline `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` markers on the enumerated seam internals (gitutil, lock, event_append, txn, purge_bridge, migration/bootstrap, reconciler git_adapter + _ref_lock)"
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope, expand the enumerated seam-internals list to include _commands/delete.py, _commands/compact.py, and _commands/fsck_repair.py (each mutates the tracker under the write lock via its own `_git`). In the Rationale, add a fourth category for ephemeral workspace provisioning (opcert_service/workspace.py, review_bot/gerrit_client.py `remote add`/`worktree add`/`checkout`) with its own marker reason, or explicitly classify those as disposable-clone sandbox writes.

findings.finding: The plan states there are exactly 'four wrapper names at HEAD (run_git, run_git_write, _run_git, _git)', but `_git` is defined in 7+ modules with different signatures/bodies; the by-name R2 rule will fire on all of them, and the plan's single-wrapper framing misrepresents the surface it must handle.
findings.location: Approach — R2 'the four wrapper names at HEAD, listed in the lint'

findings.finding: The plan asserts the old _engine/ticket_txn.py 'is deleted' and uses that to instruct authors not to enumerate ticket_txn as an entry point; the code refutes this — it still exists as a thin shim.
findings.location: Context / Problem section ("the relocated ticket_txn; the old _engine/ticket_txn.py is deleted, so ticket_txn must NOT be named as an entry point")
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to 'the transaction core was relocated to _commands/txn.py; the old _engine/ticket_txn.py remains a thin shim (until E7)' and audit that shim for a raw-git/wrapper-forward site to enumerate/mark.
